notes: source.epoch.tasks.v1 (cards T08-COMPOSE and CT23-CREDIT-ERROR-PATH): a flat-epoch plan over a real checked scoped-task region whose creator has both error edges - the creation can fail (throws<SpawnError>) and the join can observe a raised child (the worker declares throws<AllocError>), which is the edge on which the child existed and held the grant. The plan's `error(close);` declares that the creator's own error edge abandons the credit the epoch granted the creation: neither restored nor spent, credit that no exit accounts for. Refused with the exact cascade [Q635], the flat epoch's outstanding-at-the-epoch-exit band, naming the task and the abandoned figure - which is CT23's scenario, `parent abandons child-owned credit during its own error`, expected Reject. Every quantity is a DECLARED figure under the four unchanged FlatEpochBoundV1 premises (DeclaredTaskFootprints and its siblings); the checked task IR carries no credits, so the derived half is the error-edge SHAPE and the declared half is the disposition, checked against the grant the epoch actually makes. The four admitting controls pin the accounting law restored + spent = credit on every disposition including a real partial division, and the minted control pins the other refused direction (restoring more than the grant, Q636).

controls.note: The whole grant returns to the epoch on the error edge: error(move); resolved against the row's own credit clause. Admitted with restored = credit and nothing spent.
The conservative disposition, spelled: error(drop); - the creator's failure handling spends the whole grant.

Attribution: removing exactly the error(...) clause removes the refusal, and the elided arm publishes the identical all-spent split spent.qcore publishes - eliding is spelling the conservative reading, so no pre-existing epoch program changed.
Boundary: error(move 1024 effort 25); - the split is a real componentwise division of the grant, not a flag, and it adds back to the grant on both axes.

The other refused direction: error(move 8192 effort 200); restores more than the epoch ever granted, refused per task and per axis at Q636 (RestoredCreditExceedsGrant), so the error path cannot mint credit into the epoch.
